history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the Brahma Temple is not in Ajmer town - it stands at Pushkar (~15 km northwest of Ajmer), on the banks of the sacred Pushkar Lake, district Ajmer, Rajasthan. One of the very few existing temples dedicated to Brahma in India and the most prominent among them: scripture (Padma Purana) describes Pushkar as the 'king of pilgrimages' and, by Savitri's curse, the one place where Brahma may be worshipped. Legend: Brahma slew the demon Vajranabha with a lotus whose petals fell at three places, creating the Pushkar lakes; performing a yajna without his wife Savitri (he wedded Gayatri instead), she cursed him to be worshipped in Pushkar only. The marble sanctum holds a four-headed Brahma with Gayatri; the temple has a distinct red shikhara with a hamsa (swan) motif and a silver turtle embossed in the mandapa floor. The priesthood belongs to the Sanyasi (ascetic) sect, and only ascetics perform the inner-sanctum rituals. Many Pushkar temples were destroyed under Aurangzeb (1658-1707) and rebuilt; the Brahma temple's medieval structure was retained through Maharaja Jawat Raj's repairs.

name: Brahma Temple
town_description: Pushkar is a small holy town in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, built around the sacred Pushkar Lake with over 500 temples. It is one of the five sacred pilgrimage places for Hindus and hosts the famous Pushkar Camel Fair each November.
tradition: Hindu (Brahma worship; governed by the Sanyasi ascetic-sect priesthood)

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest airport (~150 km).
travel.railway: Ajmer Junction is the nearest major railway station (~15 km).
travel.road: Well connected by road from Ajmer (~15 km) and Jaipur (~150 km) via NH-48/NH-58; local buses and taxis run from Ajmer to Pushkar.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February; the Pushkar Fair around Kartik Poornima (October-November) is the peak pilgrimage season.
